text:
leo: Quick brain-dump: what if instead of copying pages to host on eviction we do transient aliasing + remap-table entries for hot shards? The idea: create a short-lived alias region in host-backed staging and update a tiny remap table so the runtime can continue using the same dptr without an expensive copy.

anya: Sounds risky. How do we handle coherence and writebacks? GPUs expect pinned device memory for kernel ops.

leo: Right. Implementation sketch: only allow aliasing for read-mostly KV slabs and readonly KV cache. For writable pages we fall back to copy-on-evict. Alias entries include mode: READ_ONLY or COHESIVE (COHESIVE requires copy-on-write). We add an epoch counter to detect stale aliases.

sri: Fragmentation angle: if aliases allocate many tiny host-backed fragments we still fragment host vaddr space. Do we pool host slabs?

leo: Yes, pool host slabs with power-of-two bucket sizes. Alias requests include preferred_bucket_hint. Remap table stores (bucket_id, offset). When alias expires we free back to bucket. That reduces external fragmentation in host arena.

pat: What's the remap-table footprint? Need to keep it tiny or else TLB warms will blow.

leo: Proposal: userspace remap cache per-GPU node with ~64k entries, each 16B -> ~1MB. Lookup is done in the runtime's lightweight path before issuing kernels; miss falls back to full translation (slow). We also expose a compact bitmap for contiguous regions for bulk-fault path.

anya: How about failure modes? If the host slab gets reclaimed we need fallback. Also we must not leak aliases across tenant boundaries.

leo: Tenant isolation: tag every remap entry with tenant_id and lease_id. Aliases are revoked on tenant tears or lease expiry. On host reclaim, allocator revokes and marks remap-miss; runtime must handle remap-miss by either re-pinning or recomputing.

sri: Telemetry ideas: remap_hit_rate, alias_expiry_count, alias_revocation_by_hostpressure, average_alias_ttl, alias_bucket_utilization.

pat: Nicely put. The big question: does this actually save latency compared to small async copies? We should benchmark: alias path vs async copy path under mixed small-read-heavy KV workload.

leo: Agree. I'll add a microbenchmark: 1) 10k small random KV reads (1-4KB), 2) 100 concurrent sessions with short seq LLMS to stress KV hits. Measure end-to-end p95 and CPU-to-GPU memcpy bytes.

anya: Security: ensure host-backed alias pages are locked (mlock) and use KMS-wrapped pointers if required by private deployments. Add audit logs for alias allocations.

leo: Config sketch (yaml):
```
staging_aliasing:
  enabled: true
  max_alias_bytes_per_gpu: 536870912   # 512MB host alias pool
  alias_ttl_secs: 10
  bucket_min_size: 4096
  bucket_max_size: 65536
  remap_table_entries: 65536
```

pat: API idea: try_alias(tenant, bytes, hints) -> {ok, alias_id, bucket_id, offset, effective_bytes, reason}. release_alias(alias_id). remap_lookup(dptr) -> {mapped, host_addr|pin_required}. Also invalidate_alias(alias_id, reason).

sri: For compaction: run bucket-level consolidation in background. We should avoid sync compaction on eviction path. If a big contiguous allocation fails, allow allocator to attempt a synchronous steal + compact only if SLA allows. Document this in escalation.

ops-bot: NOTE: canary plan needed for aliasing. Create feature flag (staging_aliasing_v1) and gate by tenant.

leo: Rollout: start with internal tenants only, A/B compare p50/p95 and memory copy bytes. If alias_revocation_by_hostpressure spikes > 1/min or remap_hit_rate < 10% disable.

anya: Tests: unit for alias lifecycle, fuzz remap-table concurrent lookups, integration with tenant teardown to ensure revocation. Also add stress test with heavy decommit on host to ensure revocation path is robust.

pat: Tracing: span for try_alias, remap_lookup hit/miss, alias_revoke, alias_release. Correlate with kernel submission latencies.

sri: One more note: expose degrade_hint in try_alias -> "reduce_prefetch" or "pin_hotset" so runtime can adjust.

leo: Good. I'll prototype allocator-side pools + remap table and a synthetic benchmark. Will open WIP PR and post link here when ready.

pat: :thumbsup: If prototype looks promising let's write a short RFC that includes security review notes and perf data.

leo: Will do. Thanks everyone.
